description: Update an athlete's profile: name, email, bio, coach notes, thresholds (partial update, e.g. just ftpWatts), the target_races list, `email_opt_out` (true stops TriPeak's emails to them, as the profile's switch does), or `rules_json` — checked rules that apply to this athlete alone. target_races is replaced whole: send every race, not only the changed one. To change one race (a priority, a date) use update_goal_race instead. A field it does not know is refused, never ignored.

athlete_id.description: May be omitted when you coach exactly one athlete.

patch.description: Fields to change. thresholds is a partial object, only the keys sent change (null clears one); its keys: ftpWatts (bike FTP, watts), weightKg (weight, kg), cssPaceSec100m (swim CSS, seconds per 100 m), runThresholdPaceSecKm (run threshold pace, seconds per km), maxHr (max heart rate, bpm), restingHr (resting heart rate, bpm), lthr (lactate threshold heart rate, bpm), cdA (aero drag area, m² (0.20–0.40)), crr (rolling resistance (0.0035–0.005)), carbsPerHour (race carb target, g/h), sex ("male" or "female"), birthYear (year of birth), poolLengthM (pool length, m (25 when unset)), wPrimeJ (W′, joules (15000–25000)). philosophy sets the coaching approach their weeks are planned under: polarised, pyramidal, threshold, sweetspot, aerobic-base or reverse (null for the app default). Writing a philosophy of the coach's own is set_training_philosophy, which validates it and selects it in one write; philosophy_custom is settable here too but has no effect on its own, because the document is only read when philosophy is 'custom'. Read tripeak://guide/philosophies before changing it — it is the coach's call, not a setting to tidy. rules_json holds the rules that are true about this athlete alone — "swims Tuesday and Thursday when the lane is free", "no more than two hard days a week" — in the same vocabulary as the coach's house rules (tripeak://guide/house-rules), and they are checked alongside them on every week written. Replaced whole, like the house rules: read the current list first. A rule that holds across the whole roster belongs in set_coaching_rules instead of being repeated on every athlete; something true about the person but not checkable — "knee has been sore since June" — belongs in notes.

name: update_athlete
